The user's question can be synthesized into: Does TDP-43 type affect the pattern of atrophy in frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD)?

Explanation:

In frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD), TDP-43 is a protein that becomes misfolded and forms toxic aggregates, leading to cell death. The progression of FTLD can vary significantly among individuals, even within the same genetic background.

Research has shown that different types of TDP-43 protein aggregation may affect the pattern of atrophy in FTLD. While there are distinct patterns of atrophy across different FTLD-TDP types, it appears that genetic and pathologic factors may also influence the progression and distribution of atrophy.

However, it is essential to note that not all patients with FTLD will exhibit a specific pattern of TDP-43 type-related atrophy, and individual results may vary. Further studies are needed to fully understand the relationship between TDP-43 type and the atrophy patterns in FTLD.

In summary, while there may be distinct patterns of atrophy related to different TDP-43 types in FTLD, it is crucial to consider that genetic and pathologic factors also play a significant role in determining the progression and distribution of atrophy.
